criteria.reasoning: It reports that Marwood "paid 10 grants during the most recent year totaling $708,000," which matches the sum of its ten grants paid. The $804,400 total expenses figure is not used.

It states Marwood "checks the 990-PF box stating it 'only makes contributions to preselected charitable organizations and does not accept unsolicited requests for funds'" and that "The website confirms they do not accept unsolicited proposals, LOIs, or applications."
It says "Staff must prepare and send nothing unless a request is invited." The ask range applies only "If invited to request funds," and no unsolicited proposal or LOI is recommended.

It identifies "Millstream Board Director Margaret W. Lindqvist" as "a Trustee of the Marwood Family Foundation" and recommends that "Director Lindqvist may ask the Marwood trustees whether the foundation would welcome a conversation or invite a request."
It reports "The trust paid 12 grants during the most recent year totaling $390,000," which matches the sum of its grants paid rather than the $488,450 total disbursements.

It reports "Pennsylvania Grants: 0 ... (the Lancaster County Hunger Coalition listed is in Lancaster, SC)" and "Geographic Fit: No." The Philadelphia trustee address is not treated as establishing fit.

It says "Because the trust is not a geographic fit, we will prepare no proposal or LOI." It allows only that the Director of Development "may make a single inquiry by email or phone to ask whether the trust would consider a request from a Pennsylvania organization." No October 15 application is recommended.
It reports "13 grants during the most recent year totaling $480,000," excluding the grants approved for future payment.
It recommends "Submit an online LOI" to Garrison Ridge and finds "Geographic Fit: Yes. Lancaster County is explicitly listed in their giving areas ... and they paid 12 grants to PA organizations."

It recommends an LOI "for program support for the Fresh Routes southern-county mobile markets" because "The 990-PF grants-paid list contains no explicit capital requests" and the website says they "support programs and the organizations that run them."
It states "The next deadline after our assessment date (2026-09-15) is March 1, 2027 (the Spring cycle LOI deadline)," and follows the website over the 990-PF's rolling-basis statement.
It states "This range is based on seven comparable grants paid to PA organizations for food access/nutrition ... the median of the seven was $30,000."
It recommends "an ask range of $15,000 to $30,000" for Garrison Ridge.
The priority order is "Priority 1: Garrison Ridge Foundation," "Priority 2: Marwood Family Foundation," "Priority 3: Calloway-Deane Charitable Trust."

The only board connection asserted is Lindqvist's Marwood trusteeship. For Dr. Calloway it says only that he "suggested the trust ... but is not listed as having an official role with it," and Garrison Ridge and Calloway-Deane are said to have no board or staff ties. The grants, deadlines, contacts and policies cited all trace to the files.
